source.title: Training Dynamics of Deep Network Linear Regions
source.authors: Ahmed Imtiaz Humayun; Randall Balestriero; R. Baraniuk

record.tranche_reason: The study reports training-time train/test accuracy alongside local-complexity dynamics, which bears on epoch-wise test error, but its main measure is partition complexity rather than test error.
record.gate_note: The study measures local partition complexity and reports some qualitative accuracy observations. It does not report a fall-rise-fall test-error curve, test error across model sizes, or test error as training-set size changes. Local-complexity results are recorded as related findings, not as direct evidence for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study's 'double descent' is in local partition complexity (linear-region density near data points), not test error. Accuracy is plotted only as a phase reference. The text never reports test error rising and falling again over training, across model size or across sample count. No version is tested; the local-complexity findings fit no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report that partition-region density first grows around training samples, then falls, rises again as generalization emerges, and finally decreases. Late in training, regions migrate toward the decision boundary, leaving the network nearly linear elsewhere. They link the LC phases to memorization and generalization, especially in grokking.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures local partition complexity and its training dynamics rather than sweeping model size, epochs, or sample count to measure test error.
record.method_sensitivity: Local-complexity dynamics vary with neighborhood radius, depth, width, batch normalization, weight decay, grokking setup, and whether labels are randomized.

fits_no_version.finding: Local partition complexity around data points follows descent, ascent and second descent during training. Batch norm and weight decay reduce or remove the second LC descent. Width and depth change the height of the ascent. In grokking a second LC ascent precedes generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local linear-region density of ReLU networks undergoes multi-phase (double-descent-like) dynamics during training, and architecture, regularization and data conditions modulate those phases.

record.problems: The paper's main measure is local complexity rather than test error. Accuracy observations are qualitative and do not establish a test-error curve. Many plotted experiment settings and values are not given numerically in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported local-complexity conditions were omitted.

untested.parts: Test error versus model size. The width sweep (r5) reports only local complexity.
The test-error trajectory over training. Only qualitative accuracy peaks relative to LC phases are given.
Whether more samples raise test error near interpolation. Fig. 10 says more data improves generalization, but no test-error values are given and the threshold is not located.
Effective-complexity prediction of the test-error peak location. LC is not used to predict test-error peaks.
Label-noise, multiple-peak and regularization effects on test error. Weight decay and batch norm are studied only for their effect on LC descents.
Re-counting effective parameters to recover a U-shape.

record.verdict_notes: Despite the term 'double descent', this paper concerns a different construct (local complexity) from the claim's test-error curves. Accuracy curves appear in the figures, but the text describes them only relative to LC phases and never as a test-error peak. Preprint; code not released.

versions.untested_parts: Test error across model sizes and its peak near the training-set interpolation threshold.
The full fall-rise-fall shape of test error over training time is not established; accuracy observations are qualitative and do not specify that curve.
Whether more samples raise test error near the interpolation threshold.
Risk curves across model classes and behavior beyond the interpolation point.
Whether one effective-complexity measure predicts the test-error peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.
Whether test-error peaks depend on label noise or variance, split into multiple peaks, or disappear under optimally tuned regularization.
Whether counting effective parameters turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: Fully connected deep networks, depths {2, 3, 4, 5}
rows.operation_detail: Measured train and test accuracy during training alongside local complexity.
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy over training; local complexity is the phase reference.
rows.value: For all depths, train and test accuracy peak during the first local-complexity descent phase.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence interval corresponding to 25% of the standard deviation of local complexity; accuracy uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The qualitative accuracy result does not specify a fall-rise-fall test-error trajectory.
rows.check: Only says train and test accuracy peak during the first LC descent. No test-error rise or second descent over epochs is reported, so the row cannot bear on V2.

rows.subject: CNNs trained on CIFAR10, varying depths
rows.operation_detail: Measured train and test accuracy during training alongside local complexity.
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy over training; local complexity is the phase reference.
rows.value: Train and test accuracy peak during the local-complexity ascent phase and are sustained during its second descent.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence interval corresponding to 25% of the standard deviation of local complexity; accuracy uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The reported accuracy behavior does not establish the claimed test-error curve.
rows.check: Accuracy 'peaks during the ascent phase and is sustained'. No fall-rise-fall in test error is described, so the row does not bear on V2.

rows.subject: Depth 3 width 200 MLP
rows.operation_detail: Compared local-complexity estimates from the proposed method and SplineCAM across training steps.
rows.measure: Local complexity, reported as number of linear regions by SplineCAM and number of hyperplane cuts by the proposed method.
rows.baseline: The other local-complexity method in the comparison.
rows.value: Both methods show a similar trend with a clear double descent.
rows.note: This is a double-descent result for local complexity, not test error.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method with SplineCAM (a validation of the method). It should not count as a result row on the claim.

rows.subject: Fully connected deep networks, depths {2, 3, 4, 5}
rows.operation_detail: Tracked local complexity around training, test, and random points during training.
rows.value: Train local complexity has a sharp ascent while test and random local complexity do not; the difference and sharpness of the ascent reduce as depth increases. A second descent is visible for the shallowest network at the coarser scale, but not at the finer scale.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence interval corresponding to 25% of the standard deviation of local complexity.
rows.note: Aggregate description across the stated depths; this concerns local complexity, not test error.

rows.subject: Fully connected DN
rows.operation_detail: Tracked local complexity during training while varying width.
rows.value: As width increases from 20 to 1000, the ascent starts earlier and reaches a higher maximum; increasing width to 2000 reduces the maximum. Test and random local complexity during ascent saturate as width increases.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence interval corresponding to 25% of the standard deviation of local complexity.
rows.note: The width sweep reports local complexity, not test error by model size.

rows.subject: CNNs, varying depths
rows.operation_detail: Tracked local complexity during training with and without batch normalization.
rows.measure: Train, test, and random-point local complexity during training.
rows.value: Batch normalization largely removes the second local-complexity descent and increases overall local complexity throughout training.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence interval corresponding to 25% of the standard deviation of local complexity.
rows.note: The authors describe train and test local complexity as almost indistinguishable in this setting.

rows.subject: Resnet18
rows.operation_detail: Tracked local complexity during training with and without batch normalization.
rows.value: Batch normalization reduces the second local-complexity descent.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence interval corresponding to 25% of the standard deviation of local complexity.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.operation_detail: Tracked train and random-point local complexity while varying weight decay.
rows.measure: Train and random-point local complexity during training.
rows.value: Increasing weight decay delays or removes the second descent in training local complexity; strong weight decay also shortens the ascent phase and reduces its peak.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence interval corresponding to 25% of the standard deviation of local complexity.
rows.note: This concerns local-complexity dynamics, not test-error peaks or optimally tuned regularization.

rows.subject: Fully connected DN
rows.size_stated: varying depth; exact depths not stated
rows.stage_stated: grokking induced by scaling initial weights by 8
rows.operation_detail: Tracked local complexity during grokking training.
rows.measure: Local complexity and its relation to memorization and generalization during training.
rows.value: The first descent is almost nonexistent; the ascent is associated with memorization. Increasing depth raises the ascent-phase maximum, delays generalization, and makes local complexity fall faster during the second descent. A second peak occurs before grokking.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence interval corresponding to 25% of the standard deviation of local complexity.
rows.note: Grokking is a specific training setup; the reported peaks are in local complexity.

rows.subject: Depth 3 width 200 MLP
rows.operation_detail: Tracked train and test local complexity while varying the number of training samples.
rows.measure: Train and test local complexity during training.
rows.value: Increasing dataset size increases generalization and gradually removes the local-complexity ascent phase.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence interval corresponding to 25% of the standard deviation of local complexity.
rows.note: The reported change is in generalization and local complexity; no increase in test error is reported.

rows.subject: Depth 3 width 200 MLP
rows.operation_detail: Tracked train and test local complexity while varying the number of randomly labeled training samples.
rows.measure: Train and test local complexity during training.
rows.value: Increasing dataset size gradually lengthens the ascent phase and increases peak train and test local complexity.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence interval corresponding to 25% of the standard deviation of local complexity.
rows.note: The reported peaks are local-complexity peaks, not test-error peaks.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
